newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, June 23 - Vancouver - GRAIN - 9 Vessels waiting, 5 loading, estimated delays of 7-10 days, depending on grain to be loaded. Roberts Bank - COAL - 2 Vessels loading, 2 waiting, 9 due to load prior to end of June, 24 scheduled for July. Prince Rupert - GRAIN - 1 Vessel loading, 2 waiting, delays of 5-7 days, depending on grade to be loaded.

HONDURAS, June 23 - Puerto Cortes - Vessels berthed, 3 discharging/loading containers, 1 loading wheat, 1 discharging wheat. Vessels awaiting berth, 2 to discharge/load containers, 1 to discharge steel rebars. Vessels due, 5 to discharge bananas, 7 to load/discharge containers, 1 passenger/vehicles, 1 to discharge corn, 1 to load crane parts. Puerto Cortes - Five vessels berthed of which 3 discharging/loading containers/generals, 1 loading zinc concentrates, 1 discharging wheat. 3 Vessels anchored of which 2 to discharge/load containers/generals. 21 Vessels due of which 1 passenger, 12 to discharge/load containers/generals, 6 to discharge/load containers/bananas, 1 to discharge fuel oil, 1 to discharge lubricants.

PANAMA, June 23 - Cristobal, Balboa - Working normally. Panama Canal - Waterway operating at full capacity. Thirty-nine vessels due, 18 in queue, 7 booked, 37 scheduled. Average of booked and non-booked canal waters time 18.1 hours.

UNITED STATES, June 23 - Port Newark, NJ - Three vessels in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Three vessels in port. Cartaret, NJ - Two vessels in port. Jersey City, Perth Amboy, Bayway, NJ - No vessels in port. Baltimore, MD - Vessels operating in port - 7 Bulkers, 4 container vessels, 2 ro/ro, 2 auto, 2 tankers, 3 general cargo, 1 cable vessel on standby. 1 Vessel in repair yard, 2 bulkers awaiting berth of which 1 to discharge sugar, 1 to discharge general. Hampton Roads, VA - Five general cargo/container vessels in pier operating, 2 bulkers in pier loading coal. 7 Anchored waiting to load, 1 tanker discharging fuel oil, 3 bulkers of which 1 each discharging cement, gypsum, 1 loading wheat, 2 vessels in shipyard under repair. Honolulu, HI - Harbour - Vessels berthed, 2 container vessels, 1 bulk carrier, 4 tugs and barges. Barbers Point, HI - Harbour - 2 Barges berthed.

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal anticipated this week. Clear at C/D canal/Baltimore harbour. Elevators and coal operations working well with no delays. Average waiting time Consol Coal 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities operating normal, no berthing congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - No vessels scheduled at either shipyard river coal terminal or the grain elevator over the next week. No delay expected at tanker terminals. All terminals up and running. Two i-high cranes to be serviced at Charleston. Columbus Street, North Charleston and Wando terminal will be light. Dredging continues in main channel with no navigation problems.

Miami, FL - No heavy traffic is expected at port of Miami and Port Everglades. Passenger terminals are available from Tuesday to Thursday. From Friday 0600 hrs. to Monday 1900 hrs. these terminals are fully operational. New York, NY - No congestion in New York anchorages, no congestion at tanker terminals and no congestion at sugar terminals. Norfolk, VA - Norfolk Southern Coal pier expecting 11 vessels during this week. Presently, 7 vessels are anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal is expecting 6 vessels. Pier IX terminal is expecting 5 vessels during the next week. Norfolk Southern Coal pier 6 will undertake a maintenance period from 10/7 to 31/7 to perform work on one of the ship loaders. During the period, one loader will be working. Cargill is not expecting any vessels during the coming week. Container and general cargo terminals are working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals are all working normally. All channels are opening, with prevailing depths available.

Philadelphia, PA - There is no port congestion in the ports of Philadelphia, Camden, Wilmington. No activity as far as dredging/repairs/navigational problems. Savannah, GA - The Georgia port authorities at Garden City terminals are forecting a busy week but no delays expected. Georgia port authorities at Ocean terminals are also forecasting a steady week with no delays expected. East Coast terminal is forecasting a steady week but no delays. Colonial Marine terminals bulk clay facility expects delays as vessels continue to wait at anchor. Savannah sugar refinery will be rather slow with only one barge expected. All bulk liquid facilities are operating normally with no congestion expected. Navigation remains normal. As the weather warms afternoon thunderstorms may cause some downtime on weather sensitive cargoes.

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion at the port of Houston City docks, Houston public grain elevator, Cargill grain elevator and Farmland grain elevator. However, congestion exists in some oil/chemical docks and private terminals for breakbulk cargo vessels. New Orleans, LA - It is normal for periods of rain to occur during summer seasons and these conditions cause delays in cargo operation especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for this season. River stage at 12.2 feet. and expected to rise to 11.6 ft. by 30 June. High river will cause delays in ship movement and vessel transit times. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi River gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Present max permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 46 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 45 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Based on these drafts we will advise all vessels to maintain sufficient airdraft for transit under bridges in Mississippi river. Some elevators are not working weekends due to slowe

WEST COAST - Columbia river - Grain vessel activity continues slow through the month of JUNE. Coos Bay - Past week busy. Two log vessels loading for discharge in Japanese ports and one lumber vessel loading metric cut lumber for Japan also. Woodchip carriers arriving at Roseburg dock, one now loading while another awaiting berth and another on its way. Only delays in vessel movement is at Roseburg woodchip terminal, no other berths experiencing congestion. No vessel delays due to weather for some time. Honolulu, HI - Vessel traffic in Honolulu and Barber's Point harbour is light for the coming week. Berths at the offport anchorages are available for bunkering vessels. Strong NE trade winds are predicted for the upcoming week and may delay vessels transiting from Asia to Hawaii. Long Beach, Los Angeles - Congestion expected in last week June particularly at Long Beach berths 212/214 bulk coal terminals. July 4 - Independence day is a longshore working holiday. July 5th - No work 0800/5th 0700/6th. Seattle
